narrative: Global markets are facing severe risk-off pressure driven by a sharp selloff in mega-cap technology and mounting geopolitical tensions. Tech shares tumbled after heavy scrutiny of massive AI infrastructure capex and weak guidance from Intel triggered an unwind of crowded hyperscaler positions. Macro headwinds are compounded by the approaching US midterm elections, where projections point toward legislative gridlock and heightened oversight. In the Middle East, an Israeli election deadlock has raised concerns over potential post-midterm military action against Iran, threatening oil supply corridors. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve held rates steady amid persistent cost-push inflation, though falling Treasury yields have provided a partial buffer via defensive rotation.

Nasdaq.why: Michael Ball highlights that the index plunged 3.5% as crowded hyperscaler positions unwound over AI capex returns, compounded by local data center pushback cited by Blair Effron.

S&P 500.why: The index breached its 100-day moving average amid Middle East war risks noted by Ethan Bronner, though Joe Mathieu notes historical gridlock and defensive rotation offer some stabilization.

Gold.why: Ethan Bronner highlights gold as a primary safe-haven beneficiary amid elevated geopolitical instability and the threat of military conflict between Israel, the US, and Iran.

Oil.why: Nathan Dean and Ethan Bronner point to substantial upside supply risks stemming from Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries and potential post-election strikes against Iran threatening the Strait of Hormuz.
